questions.question: What is celebrated on 9 January 2025 to recognise the contributions of the Indian diaspora?
questions.solution:
p-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD)** is celebrated on **9 January** every year (with a major convention every two years) to mark the contribution of the **Overseas Indian community** in the development of India.

• The date **9 January** was chosen as it was on this day in **1915** that **Mahatma Gandhi**, the greatest 'Pravasi', returned to India from **South Africa** to lead India’s freedom struggle.

• The decision to celebrate **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** was taken in accordance with recommendations of the High Level Committee (HLC) on the **Indian Diaspora** set up by the Government of India under the chairmanship of **L. M. Singhvi**.

• The first **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** was celebrated in **2003**. Since **2015**, its format has been revised to celebrate the PBD Convention once every **two years** and to hold theme-based Pravasi Bharatiya Divas Conferences during the intervening period.

• These conventions provide a platform for the **Indian diaspora** to engage with the government and the people of their ancestral land for mutually beneficial activities. ***Hence, the correct answer is Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Other Important Days in January:**

• **Army Day**: Celebrated on **15 January** every year in India, in recognition of **Field Marshal Kodandera M. Cariappa's** (then a Lieutenant General) taking over as the first Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army from General **Francis Butcher**, the last British Commander-in-Chief of India, on **15 January 1949**.

• **World Hindi Day**: Observed on **10 January** to promote the use of the **Hindi language** worldwide. It commemorates the anniversary of the first World Hindi Conference held in **Nagpur** in **1975**. This is distinct from National Hindi Divas celebrated on **September 14**.

• **National Tourism Day**: Celebrated on **25 January** in India to raise awareness about the importance of **tourism** for the country's economy and its social, political, and cultural impact.

• **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Award (PBSA):**

• The **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Award** is the highest honour conferred on a **Non-Resident Indian (NRI)**, **Person of Indian Origin (PIO)**, or an organization/institution established and run by NRIs or PIOs.

• The award is conferred by the **President of India** as a part of the **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** Convention to recognize significant contributions towards a better understanding of India abroad and support of India’s causes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas 2025:**

• The **18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** Convention is organized by the **Ministry of External Affairs** in collaboration with the State Government of **Odisha**.

• The **2025** event is scheduled to be held from **January 8 to January 10, 2025**, in **Bhubaneswar**, the capital city of **Odisha**.

• The theme for the **2025** convention focuses on the role of the **diaspora** in the era of **Viksit Bharat**, emphasizing their contribution to India’s vision of becoming a developed nation by **2047**.

3f:T

questions.question: Which pioneering molecular biologist, who co-discovered the double helix structure of DNA along with Francis H. C. Crick and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962, passed away at the age of 97 in East Northport, New York?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James D. Watson**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Dewey Watson** is an American **molecular biologist**, geneticist, and zoologist, best known for being one of the co-discoverers of the **structure of DNA** in **1953**.
 
• He, along with **Francis Crick** and **Maurice Wilkins**, was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** in **1962** for their discoveries concerning the molecular structure of nucleic acids and its significance for information transfer in living material.
 
• Watson's career was marked by his tenure at the **University of Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory**, where he collaborated with Crick to model the **double helix** structure of **Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)**.
 
• Beyond his research, he served as the **director** of the **Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL)** in **New York** for many years, significantly expanding its research in cancer and neurobiology.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the **Human Genome Project**, serving as the first director of the **National Center for Human Genome Research** at the **National Institutes of Health (NIH)** starting in **1988**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Francis H. C. Crick:**
 
 
• A British **molecular biologist** and physicist who worked closely with Watson. He is also famous for proposing the **Central Dogma** of molecular biology, which describes the flow of genetic information from **DNA to RNA to protein**.
 
 
 
• **Rosalind Franklin:**
 
 
• A British **chemist** and X-ray crystallographer whose data was critical to the discovery. Her **Photo 51**, an X-ray diffraction image of DNA, provided the essential clues for the **helical structure**. She passed away in **1958** at the **age of 37** and was not eligible for the Nobel Prize posthumously.
 
 
 
• **Maurice Wilkins:**
 
 
• A New Zealand-born British **biophysicist** who shared the **1962 Nobel Prize**. He headed the team at **King's College London** where the X-ray diffraction studies of DNA were primarily conducted.
 
 
 
• **The Double Helix Discovery:**
 
 
• The discovery published in the journal **Nature** in **April 1953** explained how genetic information is stored and replicated. It revealed that **DNA** consists of two strands winding around each other, held together by **nitrogenous bases** (Adenine, Thymine, Guanine, and Cytosine).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Academic Background:** **James Watson** earned his **Ph.D.** from **Indiana University** in **1950** at the young **age of 22**.
 
• **Literary Contribution:** He authored the best-selling book **"The Double Helix"**, published in **1968**, which provided a personal and sometimes controversial account of the race to discover DNA's structure.
 
• **Legacy:** Despite later controversies regarding his public statements, his scientific contributions remain a cornerstone of **modern biology** and **biotechnology**.
 
• **Location of Impact:** Much of his later life and administrative work was centered in **Long Island, New York**, specifically around **Cold Spring Harbor** and the surrounding **East Northport** area.
</ul

questions.question: In August 2025, who among the following chaired the Group of Ministers (GoM) that proposed exempting Goods and Services Tax (GST) on life and health insurance policies for individuals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samrat Choudhary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Group of Ministers (GoM)** on **GST** rate rationalization for insurance was chaired by **Samrat Choudhary**, who serves as the **Deputy Chief Minister of Bihar**.
 
• In **August 2025** (per the context of the legislative review), the panel proposed significant reliefs, including the exemption of **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** on premiums paid for **term life insurance** policies and **health insurance** for **senior citizens**.
 
• The **13-member GoM** was specifically constituted to address the growing demand for reducing the tax burden on essential social security products like **life and health insurance**.
 
• The committee suggested that **health insurance** premiums for individuals (other than senior citizens) should be exempted for coverage up to **Rs. 5 lakh**, while the existing **18% GST** would continue for coverage exceeding that amount.
 
• The recommendations of this **GoM** are submitted to the **GST Council**, the highest decision-making body for indirect taxes in **India**, for final approval. ***Hence, the correct answer is Samrat Choudhary.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Current GST Structure on Insurance**:
 
 
• Currently, a standard rate of **18% GST** is levied on the premium amount of most **life and health insurance** policies.
 
• Industry experts and political leaders, including **Nitin Gadkari**, had previously advocated for the removal of this tax to make insurance more affordable for the **middle class** and **underprivileged** sections.
 
 
 
• **Composition of the GoM**:
 
 
• The panel includes ministers from various states such as **Uttar Pradesh**, **Maharashtra**, **West Bengal**, **Karnataka**, **Kerala**, and **Telangana** to ensure a federal consensus.
 
• **Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka**, the Deputy CM of **Telangana**, is also a prominent member of this **Group of Ministers**.
 
 
 
• **GST Council**:
 
 
• The **GST Council** is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister** (currently **Nirmala Sitharaman**) and comprises **Finance Ministers** of all States and Union Territories.
 
• It is a constitutional body under **Article 279A** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Objective of Exemption**: The primary goal of the **Samrat Choudhary**-led panel is to boost **insurance penetration** in **India**, which remains low compared to the global average.
 
• **Financial Impact**: While the exemption reduces the tax burden on citizens, it is estimated to result in a revenue loss for the **Government**, which the **GoM** balances by looking at rate rationalization in other luxury sectors.
 
• **Term Insurance**: This is a pure risk cover where the sum assured is paid only in the event of the death of the policyholder. The **GoM** reached a consensus that this should be tax-free to encourage **financial security** for families.
 
• **Senior Citizens**: Providing **0% GST** for **senior citizens** on **health insurance** is a targeted measure to support the elderly who face higher medical costs and insurance premiums.
</ul

questions.question: Who was voted the 2024 NBA Finals most valuable player (FMVP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaylen Brown**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jaylen Brown**, the star forward for the **Boston Celtics**, was voted the **2024 NBA Finals Most Valuable Player (FMVP)** following his team's victory over the **Dallas Mavericks**.
 
• In the **2024 NBA Finals**, **Jaylen Brown** maintained an impressive average of **20.8 points**, **5.4 rebounds**, and **5.0 assists** per game across the **five-game** series.
 
• The **Boston Celtics** secured the championship title by defeating the **Dallas Mavericks** **4-1** in the series, culminating in a **106-88** win in **Game 5** on **June 17, 2024**.
 
• This victory marked the **18th** title for the **Boston Celtics**, allowing them to surpass the **Los Angeles Lakers** for the most championships in **NBA history**.
 
• **Jaylen Brown** also achieved a rare feat in **2024** by winning both the **Larry Bird Trophy** (Eastern Conference Finals MVP) and the **Bill Russell Trophy** (NBA Finals MVP) in the same postseason. ***Hence, the correct answer is Jaylen Brown.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Bill Russell NBA Finals MVP Award:**
 
 
• The award was established in **1969** and was renamed in **2009** to honor **11-time** NBA champion **Bill Russell**.
 
• The winner is selected by a panel of **11** media members who cast their votes based on performance throughout the **NBA Finals** series.
 
 
 
• **Jayson Tatum's Contribution:**
 
 
• While **Jaylen Brown** won the **FMVP**, his teammate **Jayson Tatum** became the **first player** in **Celtics** history to lead the team in **points**, **rebounds**, and **assists** during a championship-winning playoff run.
 
• In **Game 5** of the **2024** Finals, **Tatum** recorded **31 points**, **11 assists**, and **8 rebounds**.
 
 
 
• **Jaylen Brown's Career Milestones:**
 
 
• In **July 2023**, **Jaylen Brown** signed the richest contract in **NBA history** at the time, a **five-year** supermax extension worth approximately **$304 million**.
 
• Selected as the **3rd overall pick** in the **2016 NBA Draft**, **Brown** has become a **three-time NBA All-Star** (as of 2024).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Coaching History:** **Joe Mazzulla**, the head coach of the **Boston Celtics**, became the youngest coach to win an **NBA title** since **Bill Russell** (who was a player-coach) in **1969**. **Mazzulla** was **35 years old** at the time of the **2024** victory.
 
• **Series Outcome:** The **2024 NBA Finals** began on **June 6, 2024**, and concluded on **June 17, 2024**. The **Celtics** won the first three games, lost **Game 4** in **Dallas**, and closed the series at **TD Garden** in **Boston**.
 
• **Voting Breakdown:** **Jaylen Brown** received **7** out of the **11** media votes for the **FMVP**, while **Jayson Tatum** received the remaining **4** votes.
</ul

questions.question: The Van Dhan Vikas Kendra at Dugong Creek aims to make the Onge tribe self-sustainable through which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coconut-based products**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK)** at **Dugong Creek** was established specifically to cater to the socio-economic development of the **Onge tribe**, which is one of India's **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)**.
 
• The primary focus of this **VDVK** is to leverage the local availability of **coconuts** to make the tribe **self-sustainable** by producing **coconut-based products**.
 
• Under this initiative, the tribal community is trained in value-addition processes to convert raw coconuts into marketable commodities like **virgin coconut oil**, **dried copra**, and **coconut-based handicrafts**.
 
• This initiative is part of the broader **Van Dhan Yojana**, which aims to provide modern tools, equipment, and branding support to tribal gatherers so they can earn a higher share of the consumer price.
 
• By focusing on **coconut-based products**, the government ensures that the **Onge** people can utilize their traditional knowledge of the **Little Andaman** ecosystem while gaining economic independence through processed goods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Onge Tribe:**
 
 
• The **Onge** are an **Andamanese** ethnic group and are among the most primitive tribes in the world, primarily residing in **Little Andaman**.
 
• They are semi-nomadic and rely heavily on hunting, gathering, and fishing. Their population is concentrated in **Dugong Creek** and **South Bay**.
 
• Recognized as a **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG)**, the **Onge** are protected under the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956**.
 
 
 
• **Van Dhan Vikas Yojana:**
 
 
• Launched on **April 14, 2018**, by the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** and **TRIFED**, this scheme focuses on the economic empowerment of tribals through **Minor Forest Produce (MFP)**.
 
• A **Van Dhan Vikas Kendra** typically constitutes **15 tribal SHGs**, with each group comprising about **20 members**, totaling **300 beneficiaries** per Kendra.
 
• The scheme provides **Rs. 15 lakhs** for the establishment of each Kendra to cover training, basic infrastructure, and toolkits.
 
 
 
• **Location - Dugong Creek:**
 
 
• **Dugong Creek** is situated in the **Little Andaman Island** and serves as a reserved area for the **Onge** community.
 
• The area is rich in **coconut plantations**, which makes the choice of **coconut-based products** logically and economically viable for the local **VDVK** unit.
 
 
 
• **Role of TRIFED:**
 
 
• The **Tribal Co-operative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED)** is the nodal agency that provides marketing support and facilitates the sale of products through **Tribes India** outlets.
 
• It helps in **branding** and **packaging** the products made by the **Onge** tribe to meet national and international quality standards.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: How many new national records were set during the Khelo India Para Games 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The setting of **18 national records** highlights the increasing level of competitiveness and the improving quality of training and infrastructure provided to para-athletes in **India**.
 
• The event is a cornerstone of the **Khelo India** initiative, which aims to identify talent at the grassroots level and nurture it for international platforms like the **Paralympics** and **Asian Para Games**.
 
• The achievement of these records is a testament to the success of specialized schemes like the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, which supports elite athletes in their quest for excellence. ***Hence, the correct answer is 18.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2018**, the **Khelo India** programme was introduced by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** to revive the sports culture in India at the grass-root level.
 
• The **Para Games** component was added to ensure inclusivity, providing equal opportunities for **Divyang** (differently-abled) athletes to excel in a professional environment.
 
• The games focus on **12 to 15 different sporting disciplines**, including **Para Archery**, **Para Football**, and **Para Table Tennis**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Para Games:**
 
 
• The **Khelo India Para Games 2025** serves as a crucial scouting ground for the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** to identify potential medal winners for future global events.
 
• It promotes the message of "inclusive sports" and aligns with the **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016**, by fostering social integration through athletics.
 
• Financial assistance of **Rs. 5 lakhs per annum** for **8 years** is provided to selected talented players to cover their training and equipment costs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Infrastructure and Support:**
 
 
• The **2025** edition saw participation from over **2,000 athletes** representing various **States and Union Territories**.
 
• Specialized venues in **New Delhi** and other major sports hubs were equipped with **barrier-free access** and world-class equipment to facilitate high-performance results.
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** has consistently increased the budget for para-sports, reflecting in the record-breaking performances seen in the **2025** games.
 
 
 
• **Recent Achievements:**
 
 
• India's performance in international para-events has seen a steep rise following the implementation of the **Khelo India** framework, with significant medal hauls in the **Paris 2024 Paralympics** acting as a precursor to the **2025** national records.
 
• The **18 national records** set during this event serve as the new benchmarks for the next generation of **Indian para-athletes**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is one of the primary purposes of the proposed Kulsi project?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydropower generation and irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kulsi Multipurpose Project** is a major water resource initiative proposed on the **Kulsi River**, which is a significant south-bank tributary of the **Brahmaputra River**.
 
• The primary objective of the project is the **generation of hydropower** and the provision of **irrigation** facilities to enhance agricultural productivity in the region. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The project is not primarily aimed at **Military infrastructure**, as its design focuses on socio-economic development and civil utility. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While **Industrial development** might be an indirect beneficiary of the electricity generated, it is not listed as the project's primary functional purpose. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Although large water bodies often attract visitors, **Tourism promotion** is a secondary byproduct and not the core mandate like irrigation and power. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The project is planned to have an installed capacity of approximately **55 MW** of **hydropower**, contributing significantly to the energy grid of **Assam** and **Meghalaya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographic Location:** The **Kulsi River** originates in the **Khasi Hills** of **Meghalaya** and flows through the **Kamrup district** of **Assam** before joining the **Brahmaputra**. The dam site is typically proposed near **Ukiam**, located at the border of the two states.
 
• **Irrigation Scope:** The project aims to provide irrigation to over **24,000 hectares** to **40,000 hectares** of land, supporting farmers during both the **Kharif** and **Rabi** seasons.
 
• **Flood Moderation:** Apart from power and water for crops, the project serves the critical function of **flood control**. It helps in regulating the discharge of water during the heavy **Monsoon** months, reducing the risk of downstream flooding in **Assam**.
 
• **National Project Status:** Due to its scale and regional importance, the **Kulsi Project** has been considered for **National Project** status, which allows for a **90:10** funding pattern between the **Central Government** and the state.
 
• **Environmental Significance:** The river is one of the few remaining habitats for the endangered **Gangetic River Dolphin** (Platanista gangetica), making the ecological impact assessment of this project a vital administrative and environmental concern.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementing Agencies:** The project planning and Detailed Project Reports (DPR) are often handled by the **Brahmaputra Board** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, Government of India.
 
• **Inter-state Coordination:** Since the river flows through both **Assam** and **Meghalaya**, the project requires a high degree of cooperation regarding land acquisition and benefit-sharing between the two state governments.
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact:** By providing stable **electricity** and **water**, the project is expected to boost the local economy, improve **livelihoods**, and provide a buffer against the erratic nature of rainfall in the **North-Eastern** region of **India**.
</ul

questions.question: Inaugurated in September 2025, the Monopropellant Thruster Test Facility (MPTTF) primarily supports testing activities related to which broad technological domain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Space propulsion systems**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Monopropellant Thruster Test Facility (MPTTF)** was officially inaugurated in **September 2025** to serve as a specialized hub for evaluating advanced **Space propulsion systems**.
 
• The facility is primarily designed to conduct rigorous testing of **low-thrust monopropellant engines**, which are essential for the **Reaction Control Systems (RCS)** and **Attitude and Orbit Control Systems (AOCS)** of various spacecraft.
 
• Equipped with high-performance **vacuum chambers**, the MPTTF can simulate the extreme conditions of **outer space**, allowing engineers to measure critical parameters such as **Specific Impulse (Isp)**, **Thrust**, and **Thermal Management**.
 
• The establishment of this facility marks a significant milestone in achieving **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) in the space sector, reducing dependency on international testing labs for **satellite propulsion** validation.
 
• Testing at MPTTF focuses on the reliability of **catalyst beds** and **propellant feed systems**, ensuring that thrusters can perform thousands of **pulses** over a mission lifespan of **10 to 15 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monopropellant Technology:**
 
 
• A **monopropellant** is a chemical propellant that consists of a single substance or a mixture of chemicals that decomposes or reacts when exposed to a **catalyst**.
 
• Unlike bipropellant systems, it does not require a separate **oxidizer**, making the propulsion system simpler, lighter, and more **reliable**.
 
• **Anhydrous Hydrazine** is the most commonly used monopropellant in the industry due to its stable storage and predictable performance characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Satellites:**
 
 
• These systems are vital for **Station Keeping** (maintaining the satellite's assigned position in orbit) and **Momentum Dumping**.
 
• They are extensively used in **Geostationary Satellites (GEO)** and **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** constellations for precise **manoeuvring**.
 
 
 
• **Emerging Green Propellants:**
 
 
• Modern facilities like MPTTF are increasingly being adapted to test **Green Propellants** such as **Hydroxylammonium Nitrate (HAN)** and **Ammonium Dinitramide (ADN)**.
 
• These alternatives are **less toxic** and more environmentally friendly compared to traditional **Hydrazine**, reducing the **hazard costs** associated with fueling operations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Precision Testing:** The facility can measure very small thrust values, often in the range of **1 Newton to 22 Newtons**, which are standard for **Micro-satellites** and **Nano-satellites**.
 
• **Operational Readiness:** By providing a localized testing environment, the facility accelerates the **Time-to-Market** for private space startups and **Government space agencies**.
 
• **Data Acquisition:** It utilizes high-speed **data acquisition systems** to monitor the **catalytic decomposition** process, which occurs at temperatures exceeding **800 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** The MPTTF supports the growth of the **Commercial Space** sector, particularly in the development of **satellite buses** for global customers under the **NewSpace India** initiatives.
</ul

questions.question: Which category of climate finance did India argue should be scaled up *independently* during the post-COP-30 negotiations held in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adaptation finance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the post-**COP-30** negotiations held in **November 2025**, **India** strongly advocated for the **independent scaling up** of **Adaptation finance**. **India** argued that funding for building resilience must be distinct and not overshadowed by **mitigation** efforts.
 
• The demand was made in the context of the **New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG)**, which is the new financial target intended to succeed the **$100 billion** annual pledge made by developed nations. **India** emphasized that **adaptation** is a matter of survival for **developing countries** and requires predictable, grant-based public funding.
 
• **India** pointed out that **adaptation** projects often lack the commercial appeal of **mitigation** (such as **renewable energy**), making it difficult to attract private capital. Therefore, a separate and **scaled-up** allocation is necessary to address the specific needs of the **Global South**.
 
• The negotiations highlighted the **doubling of adaptation finance** pledge made at **COP-26** in **Glasgow**, with **India** insisting that this target must be met and significantly expanded post-**2025**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Adaptation finance.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Adaptation vs. Mitigation:** 
 
 
• **Mitigation** refers to efforts to reduce or prevent the emission of **greenhouse gases**, such as transitioning to **solar** or **wind energy**.
 
• **Adaptation** involves taking action to prepare for and adjust to both the current effects of **climate change** and the predicted impacts in the future, such as building **flood defenses** or developing **drought-resistant crops**.
 
 
 
• **COP-30 (Conference of the Parties):** 
 
 
• The **30th United Nations Climate Change Conference** took place in **Belém, Brazil**, in **November 2025**. It was a landmark summit focusing on the **Amazon rainforest** and the **Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA)**.
 
• The summit aimed to finalize the **NCQG**, ensuring that trillions of dollars are mobilized for **climate action** in **vulnerable nations**.
 
 
 
• **Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA):** 
 
 
• Established under the **Paris Agreement** (**Article 7**), the **GGA** aims to enhance adaptive capacity, strengthen resilience, and reduce vulnerability to **climate change**.
 
• During **2024-2025**, the focus shifted toward establishing clear indicators to measure progress in **adaptation** globally.
 
 
 
• **India's Domestic Framework:** 
 
 
• **India** implements its **adaptation** strategies through the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**, which includes **eight national missions** covering water, agriculture, and Himalayan ecosystems.
 
• The **National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC)** was established in **2015-16** to assist states and union territories that are particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of **climate change**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Loss and Damage Finance:** Unlike **adaptation** (which is proactive), **Loss and Damage** finance refers to compensation for the unavoidable and irreversible impacts of **climate change** that have already occurred. The **Loss and Damage Fund** was operationalized at **COP-28**.
 
• **Climate Finance Gap:** The **UNEP Adaptation Gap Report** frequently highlights that the costs of **adaptation** in **developing countries** are **5 to 10 times** greater than current public **adaptation finance** flows.
 
• **CBDR-RC:** **India’s** stance is rooted in the principle of **Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)**, which holds **developed countries** historically responsible for **emissions** and thus obligated to provide **financial resources**.
 
• **Article 9 of the Paris Agreement:** This article stipulates that **developed country Parties** shall provide **financial resources** to assist **developing country Parties** with respect to both **mitigation** and **adaptation**.

questions.question: Which Vietnamese-American author released 'The Emperor of Gladness' in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ocean Vuong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ocean Vuong**, a celebrated **Vietnamese-American** author, is the creator of the novel titled **'The Emperor of Gladness'**, which saw its release in **May 2025**.
 
• The book is a highly anticipated work of fiction following his monumental success in both the realms of **poetry** and **prose**.
 
• The narrative of **'The Emperor of Gladness'** focuses on the relationship between a young man and an elderly person struggling with **memory loss**, exploring themes of care, loneliness, and human connection.
 
• **Ocean Vuong** has established himself as a prominent voice in contemporary **American literature**, known for his lyrical and emotionally resonant writing style that often bridges his identity as a **poet** with his narrative storytelling. ***Hence, the statement regarding his authorship of this book is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Literary Career and Major Works:**
 
 
• **Ocean Vuong** gained international acclaim with his debut novel, **'On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous'**, published in **2019**. The novel is framed as a letter from a son to his illiterate mother and explores the legacy of the **Vietnam War**.
 
• In the field of poetry, his collection **'Night Sky with Exit Wounds'** (**2016**) won the **T.S. Eliot Prize** and the **Whiting Award**.
 
• His subsequent poetry collection, **'Time is a Mother'**, was released in **2022**, further cementing his reputation for exploring grief and family history.
 
 
 
• **Biography and Background:**
 
 
• Born in **1988** in **Saigon, Vietnam** (now **Ho Chi Minh City**), he immigrated to the **United States** at the **age of two** after spending time in a **refugee camp** in **the Philippines**.
 
• He grew up in **Hartford, Connecticut**, and his experiences as a **first-generation immigrant** and a **queer man** of color are central themes in his literary output.
 
• In **2019**, he was awarded the prestigious **MacArthur Fellowship**, commonly known as the **"Genius Grant,"** for his contributions to literature.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Colum McCann**: An **Irish** writer known for novels like **'Let the Great World Spin'** and **'Apeirogon'**.
 
• **Charlotte McConaghy**: An **Australian** author recognized for her works **'Migrations'** and **'Once There Were Wolves'**, which often focus on environmental and nature-driven themes.
 
• **Sharon Lee**: Often associated with **science fiction** and the **Liaden universe** series, representing a different genre entirely from Vuong's literary fiction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Theme of the Book:** The novel **'The Emperor of Gladness'** signifies a shift or continuation in Vuong's exploration of **vulnerability** and **intergenerational bonds**.
 
• **Release Timeline:** The **May 2025** release was one of the most significant literary events of the year, highlighting the enduring popularity of **Asian-American** narratives in the global market.
 
• **Style:** Vuong is often cited for his **autofictional** elements, though his **2025** release demonstrates a deepening of his fictional world-building and character studies.
</ul
